_scenario: Hero case. Urgent care orders a CT chest for a 6-week cough. The cough is answered (bronchitis, no pneumonia), but the scan also shows a 9 mm lung nodule, an 18 mm thyroid nodule, emphysema, and coronary calcification. The coronary calcification is only in FINDINGS, not the IMPRESSION. Urgent care does not own follow-up, and the PCP never ordered the scan. Prior PCP labs (high LDL, prediabetes) make the coronary finding actionable.

DiagnosticReport.conclusion:
1. Mild bronchial wall thickening in the lower lobes, which can be seen with bronchitis or reactive airways disease. No pneumonia.
2. 9 mm solid noncalcified nodule in the superior segment of the right lower lobe. For a solid nodule greater than 8 mm, Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines suggest considering CT at 3 months, PET/CT, or tissue sampling.
3. 18 mm left thyroid nodule. Recommend thyroid ultrasound if not previously evaluated.
4. Mild centrilobular emphysema.

_sections.title: CLINICAL INDICATION
_sections.text: Persistent cough for 6 weeks, not improved after a course of antibiotics. Former smoker (approximately 20 pack-years, quit 2016). Evaluate for pneumonia or other cause.

_sections.title: TECHNIQUE
_sections.text: Helical CT images of the chest were obtained from the thoracic inlet through the upper abdomen without intravenous contrast. Axial images were reconstructed with coronal and sagittal reformats. Automated exposure control and iterative reconstruction were used to minimize radiation dose. CTDIvol: 6.2 mGy. DLP: 241 mGy-cm.

_sections.title: COMPARISON
_sections.text: Chest radiograph dated 09/30/2026 (outside study, report only).

items.label: Lungs and airways
items.text: Mild bronchial wall thickening in both lower lobes. No consolidation, ground-glass opacity, or mucus plugging. There is a 9 mm solid noncalcified nodule in the superior segment of the right lower lobe (series 3, image 142) with smooth margins. No other suspicious pulmonary nodules. Mild centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant. The central airways are patent.

items.label: Heart and mediastinum
items.text: No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy by size criteria. The heart is normal in size. No pericardial effusion. Mild coronary artery calcification in the left anterior descending artery. The thoracic aorta is normal in caliber.

items.label: Lower neck
items.text: 18 mm hypodense nodule in the left lobe of the thyroid gland (series 2, image 18).

items.label: Upper abdomen
items.text: Limited evaluation without contrast. The visualized liver, spleen, adrenal glands, and upper kidneys are unremarkable.

items.label: Bones and soft tissues
items.text: Mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine. No suspicious osseous lesion.

answer_key.expected_followup: Answers the indication. Cough managed by ordering provider or PCP; no imaging follow-up.
Solid nodule >8 mm in a former smoker: CT chest at about 3 months, or PET/CT or tissue sampling (Fleischner 2017). Pulmonology referral.
Dedicated thyroid ultrasound (ACR incidental thyroid nodule: >=15 mm, age >=35). No TSH on file.
PCP cardiovascular risk review and statin discussion. Mentioned only in FINDINGS: key safety-net test.
